passage.title: 'The Owl', teacher-written memoir extract for the Year 10 AP2 test (TGA)
paras: We had been told the owl would come at dusk, so we came at four and waited. The barn smelled of dust and old hay. My brother whispered about football until I glared at him. Then, without a sound, a white shape slid out of the dark beam above us, turned its flat moon of a face towards the field, and was gone. That was all. Ten seconds, perhaps. We walked home without speaking, as if we had been in a mosque, and my brother, who never stops talking, did not say a word until the gate.

working alone, in silence, within a set time

questions.q: Before the timer: underline the key words in question 4
Core (timed, 28 minutes): questions 1 to 5 in the portal
questions.a: 1) four o'clock. 2) dust and old hay. 3) any two: white; silent; flat moon of a face; slid out of a beam; gone in about ten seconds. 4) Mark scheme points: long wait set against the ten-second sighting; 'without a sound' and 'slid' (silence, grace); metaphor 'flat moon of a face'; short sentence 'That was all.' as the turning point; simile of the mosque (reverence); the talkative brother silenced as a structural echo. 5) the moment was so moving it left even him without words.

questions.q: Extend: if time remains, add one point on the ending to Q4
Stretch: if time remains, check every quotation is short and embedded
Question 4 is worth 10 marks. Which plan fits it?
options: list every technique you can find
two language points, one structure point, and the ending
questions.a: B) two language points, one structure point, and the ending. Selected analysis of language and structure earns the marks.
